Unlawful homicide by a minister abroad is not an act jure imperii; it is a private criminal act, so it is treated as jure gestionis or, more precisely, as not attributable to the state as a sovereign act at all. It therefore enjoys no state immunity ratione materiae as an official act. However, the note's claim that a foreign court may hear any case against a minister whatever the nature of the act is too broad, since immunity ratione personae can still bar proceedings in foreign courts while the minister holds office.
CONFIDENCE: 88
